query: What patient needs appear in visit notes?

per_column.name: clinical_problem_type
per_column.rationale: The nature of the clinical problem (acute, chronic, preventive, etc.) is a constitutive aspect of what a patient needs -- it characterizes the underlying need itself, not an external correlate.

per_column.name: acuity_and_threat
per_column.rationale: The urgency/severity dimension of a patient's need is a genuine aspect of the need (how pressing the need is). It is a part-of decomposition, though it overlaps somewhat with the existing 'urgency' column and with clinical_problem_type's acute/chronic split.

per_column.name: intervention_required
per_column.rationale: What intervention the patient requires (pharmaceutical, procedural, counseling) directly expresses the substance of the need -- what must be done for the patient. A legitimate facet.

per_column.name: anatomic_system_focus
per_column.rationale: Which body system/domain the need concerns is an aspect of the need (its clinical locus). Constitutive, though values mixing anatomic systems with 'mental_health' and 'pediatric_developmental' blur the facet's basis.

per_column.name: care_coordination_requirement
per_column.rationale: The coordination/follow-up a patient's care requires is a real aspect of the need -- the ongoing/logistical dimension. A distinct part-of facet.

judge.rationale: All five columns are genuine part-of facets of 'patient_needs' (problem nature, acuity, required intervention, anatomic locus, and coordination requirement), so the meronymy test is satisfied across the board. Mutual exclusivity is good but not perfect: acuity_and_threat partly overlaps with the acute/chronic distinction embedded in clinical_problem_type, and anatomic_system_focus imports a 'mental_health' value that also appears in clinical_problem_type, creating cross-facet redundancy. Exhaustiveness is strong -- the set spans the problem, its severity, its treatment, its bodily domain, and its downstream coordination -- though patient-experienced/psychosocial or informational needs (e.g., patient understanding, social/support needs) are underrepresented, leaving some constitutive aspects only partially covered.
